questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can choose either off-campus hall or on-campus halls, but the allocation is random.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a shared kitchen in the hall.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The exchange students are provided with double rooms. You need to share the bedroom with another student. I would rather recommend choosing the off-campus hall (JCH). Because it is close to the shopping malls and the subway, making transportation more convenient. Moreover, the facilities there are new. If you want to explore Hong Kong, I think JCH is a better choice.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For MA students, registering for courses at HKUST is not easy. All exchange students are registered as BA students. If you want to register for MA courses, you must apply on the system and obtain approval from the instructors. However, some MA courses instructors seem not to be welcoming of exchange students. They either reject the applications or completely ignore the emails. At the beginning of the semester, I spent a lot of time connecting with the instructors to register for MA courses, and the registration time was very limited, which put me a lot of pressure. I contacted over 10 instructors, but only received approval from 3 of them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Ask them by email or phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan in advance the courses you wish to register for, and also think about alternative courses.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For economics students, I would recommend ECON5210 Microeconomic Theory. The course content is quite challenging and it is actually a PhD-level course. However, the instructor teaches very well and even some undergraduate students choose this course. The course design is reasonable and I have learned a lot from it.
